topic: Killingham's offensive self-love is the mirror of Sanji's self-neglect, which is why his Dream Output targets Sanji's weakness
title: Killingham Loves Himself Too Much, Sanji Too Little
description: Sanji versus Killingham in chapters 1196 and 1197 is a fight between two kinds of self-love. Killingham's nightmare power only works on a man who ranks himself last. Which side of the mirror is Oda on?
comment: Is Killingham's self-love the real villain trait here, or is it Sanji's habit of putting himself last? Pick one.
end_text: WHY ODA GAVE SANJI THIS HAKI

lines.text: Killingham loves himself too much, and Sanji loves himself too little.

shot.fallback: masked knight facing a blond cook in the snow

lines.text: He treats his own worth like armor, and then he swings it at everybody else.

shot.fallback: knight in black armor swinging a spear

lines.text: In chapter 1196, his Dream Output ability drags a nightmare version of Ivankov out of Sanji's head.

shot.fallback: knight conjuring a looming dark figure

lines.text: He doesn't hit Sanji's body first. He goes after what Sanji believes about himself.

shot.fallback: cook staring up at a dark figure

lines.text: That only works on someone who ranks himself last, and Sanji has proven that for years.

shot.fallback: cook diving to protect his captain

lines.text: The villain built his whole attack on the exact crack Ivankov warned about at the end of chapter 1195.

shot.fallback: tall queen warning a young cook

lines.text: And the counter isn't loving less. It's loving himself enough to count too. That's what Love Is Defense means.

shot.fallback: cook with a determined smile and flames
